answer: An identity claiming a jetty breakwater section posts an 85-credit bond and places basalt units marked with a pigment batch code, filing its placement count. The fee starts at 31 credits and rises per filing, so the kth filing costs 31+7(k-1); the 1000th costs 7024, and 1,000 fake filings cost 3,527,500 plus 85,000 locked. An auditor recomputes coverage from the placement log against the design plan; a shortfall burns the bond. A rented-unit ring fails because a pigment batch code is bound to one section key, so a code reused in a second section burns both bonds. Honest builders pay 31 once.
